title: Youth shelter security and winter homelessness response
subtitle: Warming centre hours, shelter site security funding in 2023 budget, and coordination with area municipalities
overview: The Community and Health Services Committee heard from the CEO of oneROOF Youth Services, who asked for funding for full-time in-house security at the Kitchener site. The agency reported a sharp rise in critical incidents involving off-site adults since December 2022 and linked it to the nearby emergency shelter in the former Kitchener Schwaben Club. Staff said the Region already provides 24-hour security at shelter sites it legally owns, but no funding exists for security in surrounding neighbourhoods.

No motion was moved on this item. The committee directed staff to review urgent security concerns at all Regional shelter sites and the chance of security funding in the 2023 budget, considering community resources that may apply. Staff also committed to meet the agency soon about short-term options.

On the interim housing update, the committee thanked staff for their work during the severe weather before Christmas 2022. It directed staff to look at extending warming centre hours and to debrief with area municipalities on coordinating weather responses. The committee received the report for information {{vote:m1}}.

decisions.detail: The committee received the interim housing solutions implementation update for information as part of the consent agenda {{vote:m1}}.

debate: The delegate argued that youth distrust outside security staff, so funding should go to in-house staff seen as part of the youth shift team. The delegate also said neighbour complaints had risen again and that the housing arrangements limit how adult guests can be handled.

Staff said security is built into contracts for Region-owned shelter sites, but the funding envelope cannot cover neighbourhood-wide security. Staff said security is not a cure-all and every security dollar is one not spent elsewhere. They offered to raise it in budget talks with funded providers.

Several councillors asked where police fit in, and whether other agencies should be involved. Others cautioned that more policing is costly and can criminalize vulnerable people, and called for a broad definition of security, including mental health or social supports.

One councillor was concerned that the budget process could take another month or two while incidents continue, and asked for a more immediate response. Others asked that staff also consider the effects on neighbourhoods around all shelter sites and youth needs in Cambridge.

On winter weather, one councillor asked whether warming centres could run around the clock rather than closing in the late afternoon. Another asked that area municipalities be included in a debrief, and staff agreed.
